note: massFull_t is the mass with full consumables (fuel/oil/sand/water/coal) and is what actually rolls. ratedLoad_t comes from the community empirical test on the Harbour reference climb, not from the in-game Vehicle Catalog: see DATA-SOURCES.md. refSpeed_kmh is the sustained speed recorded at test point L3 with that load.

locomotives.name: DE2-480 Shunter
locomotives.notes: Passive traction-motor cooling: cooling comes from airflow, so slowing down on a climb starts a heat-death spiral. Carry speed into the grade.

locomotives.name: DM3-540 Diesel Shunter
locomotives.notes: Enormous torque in low gear but adhesion-limited: the rated load is only reachable with sand at walking pace. Derate 30-50% for sustained climbs. Mechanically coupled engine means downhill speed must be controlled or the engine over-revs.

locomotives.name: DH4-670 Road-Switcher
locomotives.notes: Struggles to accelerate past ~50 km/h in third converter. Sometimes downshifts late at the foot of a climb and loses momentum.

locomotives.name: DE6-860
locomotives.notes: Rheostatic dynamic brake peaks at 35 km/h. Not remote-capable on its own, but inherits the remote through an MU cable to a DE2 or DH4.

locomotives.name: S060-440 Steam Shunter
locomotives.notes: 0-6-0, so all weight is adhesive. Small water tank: range, not tractive effort, is usually the binding constraint on a long haul.

locomotives.name: S282-730
locomotives.notes: 2-8-2: only the four coupled driving axles carry adhesive weight, and the tender carries none. adhesiveMass_t is an estimate, not a measured figure.

locomotives.name: BE2-260 Microshunter
locomotives.notes: Yard and turntable duty only. Destroys its drivetrain above 45 km/h even when towed dead. The wiki infobox lists an 800 t load rating that contradicts every measured figure and the article's own text; this dataset uses the measured 100 t.
